headline: Foundation Stone Laid for ‘Healing Fins’ – Maharashtra’s First Multispecialty Fish Clinic & Mobile Fish Care Unit at ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai | ICAR
content: The Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony of “Healing Fins” – Maharashtra’s First Multispecialty Fish Clinic & Mobile Fish Care Unit was held today, at the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Education, Mumbai. The foundation stone was laid by the Chief Guest, Advocate Ashish Shelar, Minister of Information Technology & Cultural Affairs and Guardian Minister, Mumbai Suburban, Government of Maharashtra. The ceremony was graced by Haroon Rashid Khan, Member of Legislative Assembly, Versova Constituency; Saurabh Katiyar, District Collector, Mumbai Suburban; Sanjay Kumar Shinde; and N. P. Sahu, Director, ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai, along with other dignitaries. The “Healing Fins” facility is being established within the ICAR-CIFE campus by the Aquatic Environment and Health Management (AEHM) Division, with financial support from the District Planning Committee, Mumbai Suburban, Government of Maharashtra. Located at Versova, the facility aims to provide comprehensive fish health services, including disease diagnosis and treatment, catering to fish farmers, shrimp farmers, aquarium owners, and ornamental fish hobbyists. The initiative adopts a four-tier approach encompassing clinical services, mobile outreach, advanced diagnostics, and telehealth services to ensure holistic fish health management. A Mobile Fish Care Unit has also been integrated to deliver on-site services, enabling timely treatment and technical advisory support at farm and field levels. The programme commenced with a welcome address by Dr. N. P. Sahu, who highlighted the significance of the initiative. This was followed by a detailed presentation by Megha K. Bedekar, Principal Scientist, Head of AEHM Division, and Principal Investigator of the project, who elaborated on the concept, infrastructure, and operational framework of the clinic and mobile unit. During the programme, Shri Haroon Rashid Khan underscored the importance of establishing such a facility in a metropolitan region and its potential benefits to stakeholders in the fisheries sector. The dignitaries also visited key facilities of ICAR-CIFE, including the Aquatic Biodiversity Museum and Aquarium, and appreciated the institute’s contributions to fisheries education, research, and extension. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Aishwarya Ranadive, Assistant Commissioner of Fisheries, Mumbai Suburban. The event witnessed the participation of more than 250 attendees, including Heads of Divisions, scientists, students, representatives of fishermen societies, and staff of the Mumbai Suburban Committee.

headline: Row over power purchase snowballing in Keralam
content: Thiruvananthapuram: The opposition CPI(M) in Keralam has raised suspicion of corruption in the Congress government's decision to purchase power from GNA Energy, a Haryana based OTC platform, overlooking an offer from Himachal Pradesh. Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan even alleged that an artificial power crisis was being created to purchase power at higher price even as power at lower rates would be available in view of the rains received in many states. .Soaring heat, inadequate rains plunge Kerala into acute crisis: State imposes up to one hour power cuts.Vijayan also said that the decision to purchase power from an OTC platform instead of a producer also deepens the mystery as private power producers could be getting the benefit of the deal. The differences within the Congress government over the economic viability of the power purchase is also helping the opposition to step up the attack against the V D Satheesan government. Meanwhile, Satheesan denied Vijayan's allegations and maintained that while considering the average price of the power during the peak hours and non peak hours the offer by GNA was more viable. He also said that even the previous left front government had purchased power from the same firm. He also denied the allegations that the power crisis was an artificial one by citing reports. The fresh row was triggered after a report of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) citing the purchasing power from GNA would lead to an additional financial burden of Rs. 726 crore compared to that from Himachal. KSEB also cited that Himachal's proposal would also help in addressing the peak hour shortage GNA has offered round the clock supply of 500 MW at Rs. 8.48 per unit. KSEB cited that it could lead to surplus power during day time. Himachal had offered power at Rs. 14.50 per unit, which KSEB was hopeful of reducing to Rs. 12.50 per unit through negotiations. The Chief Minister's justification was that considering the average costs, the one by GNA would be more profitable for the state even if there is surplus during the day time.

headline: Supreme Court settles decade-old energy dispute, Himachal to get 11,973 MU electricity from Punjab, Haryana
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday brought the curtain down on a decades-long energy dispute between Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Haryana over the payment of dues arising from Bhakra Beas Management Board projects since 1966. .A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana accepted the Centre’s cashless proposal on payment of dues in energy terms to Himachal Pradesh by Punjab and Haryana. .The top court said the arrangement will be as per a 2011 apex court verdict settling power dues arising out of Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydro projects since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh at the rate of 7.19 per cent. .Cannot convict one accused alone under common intention charge when co-accused are acquitted: Supreme Court.It said Punjab and Haryana will pay Himachal Pradesh 11,973 million units of electricity over a period of 20 years. .Punjab government initially opposed the Centre’s proposal for payment of energy arrears in 15 years but later sought implementation of the plan over a period of 30 years, while Himachal Pradesh sought implementation within 10 years. .Under the proposal, an adjustment of Rs 420 crore towards historical capital costs incurred in constructing the dams has been factored into the settlement, and Himachal Pradesh will not have to pay anything to Punjab and Haryana. .The original entitlement was calculated at 13,066 million units by the Central Electricity Authority. .According to the 2011 decision of the apex court, the share of Himachal was fixed at 7.19 per cent, while that of Punjab and Haryana was fixed at 51.80 per cent and 37.51 per cent, respectively. .Rajasthan's share largely remained unaffected, while the share of Chandigarh was fixed at 3.50 per cent. .According to the 2011 decision, Himachal was to get a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977, and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.

headline: Aarti Drugs' Baddi facility in Himachal Pradesh gets 3 US FDA Form 483 observations
content: Aarti Drugs Ltd on Friday said its subsidiary, Pinnacle Life Science Private Ltd, received three inspectional observations in Form 483 from the United States Food and Drug Administration following an inspection of its formulations manufacturing facility in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh.The US FDA inspected the facility from November 2 to November 6, 2026. Aarti Drugs said none of the three observations was related to data integrity and that the company would work closely with the US regulator to resolve all the points.In a regulatory filing, Aarti Drugs said the observations would have no impact on the financial, operational or other activities of the company. It also stated that there was no financial or operational impact on Pinnacle Life Science. The company received the Form 483 communication on November 6, the date on which the inspection concluded.ALSO READ | Aarti Drugs Q2 Results: Net profit soars 83% on stronger margins, revenue growthAarti Drugs said it would work closely with the US FDA to address the three inspectional observations received at the conclusion of the inspection. The company did not specify the individual observations in its filing. It reiterated that none of the points was related to data integrity.What is a Form 483A Form 483 is a list of observations made during the inspection and is issued by the USFDA inspectors post the completion of the inspection. The inspector will communicate and explain these observations to the supplier during the closing conference. But a Form 483 does not represent a final FDA determination regarding the facility’s GMP compliance.Post Form 483 is issued, the company is given 15 days time to submit its response to the USFDA explaining what steps will the company take to resolve the observations made by USFDA.ALSO READ | Aarti Drugs sees healthy FY27 growth as prices remain firm, capacity expandsShares of Aarti Drugs Ltd ended at ₹445.90, up by ₹1.60, or 0.36%, on the BSE.

headline: Immunologist Manali Mukherjee receives Falling Walls Women's Impact Award for her work on Long Covid
content: The prestigious international award recognizes Mukherjee’s patient-centred, evidence-based research on Long COVID. McMaster respiratory immunologist Manali Mukherjee has been honoured at the 2026 Falling Walls Science Summit in Berlin for research that reveals the biological basis of Long COVID. Mukherjee, an associate professor of medicine, is a 2026 Falling Walls Winner in the Women’s Impact Award category and a Science Breakthrough of the Year winner for her work, “Breaking the Wall of Long COVID Denial: With Immunology, Not Opinion.” The societal and institutional fatigue linked to the pandemic has curtailed research around the long-term impacts of COVID-19 on patients, some of whom developed autoimmune diseases after being perfectly healthy prior to their illness, said Mukherjee, who is also the AstraZeneca Chair in Respiratory Diseases. “The only fatigue that should be associated with Long COVID is the fatigue of the people who are suffering from it,” said Mukherjee. “That’s the fatigue we should be addressing. There should not be fatigue in policymakers or those responsible for funding and conducting research.”

headline: CM’s constituency visits political drama, won’t save Cong govt: BJP
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh BJP on Friday accused chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu of resorting to “political drama” through constituency visits and multi-crore announcements ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, alleging that the Congress govt had lost public confidence.Addressing a news conference, BJP state media in charge and Naina Devi MLA Randhir Sharma questioned the financial credibility of the announcements, claiming govt lacked funds for basic road repairs, HRTC bus maintenance and MLA development works. He also demanded details of budgetary provisions for the new promises.Accusing the state govt of corruption and diversion of disaster relief funds, Sharma demanded a white paper detailing central assistance received under the SDRF (State Disaster Response Fund), the NDRF (National Disaster Response Fund) and the PDNA (Post Disaster Needs Assessment), along with department-wise allocations, constituency-wise expenditure, contractors and payments.He claimed Rs 2,006 crore had been approved under the PDNA, including a central share of Rs 1,504 crore, of which Rs 1,053 crore was released in July and Dec 2025.Sharma also alleged irregularities in public works department tendering and political discrimination in reconstruction works, demanding an independent probe into payments allegedly made without execution of work.On the Supreme Court’s verdict on the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), Sharma said it was the result of successive govts’ efforts since 1996 and not any single regime’s achievement.He also opposed the proposed public-private partnership (PPP) transfer of Hotel Peterhof in Shimla.The BJP functionary further questioned unfulfilled Congress guarantees, including Rs 1,500 monthly assistance for women and 300 units of free electricity. headline: Himachal CM Sukhu presides over ‘Sarkar Gaon Ke Dwaar’ programme at Mehla in Chamba
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 6 (ANI): Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu presided over the ‘Sarkar Gaon Ke Dwaar’ programme at Mehla, a remote village of Mehla Gram Panchayat in the Bharmaur assembly constituency of Chamba district. He stayed overnight in the village on Thursday evening and interacted with the local people, Mahila Mandals and Yuvak Mandals. He listened to the grievances of the people and directed the officials to ensure their prompt resolution.Dressed in traditional attire, the local residents accorded a warm welcome to the Chief Minister upon his arrival in Mehla gram panchayat, accompanied by the melodies of traditional hill folk tunes. It proved to be a memorable evening for them, as it was the first time a Chief Minister stayed overnight in this remote region, taking the opportunity to learn about their problems and challenges. He also enjoyed the local delicacies offered by the residents. ‘Visits to the remote villages and overnight stays are aimed at gaining first-hand insight into the challenges being faced by local residents and understanding their concerns,’ said the Chief Minister while interacting with the villagers.CM Sukhu said that ‘Sarkar Gaon Ke Dwar’ was a flagship programme of the state government, with resolution of public grievances being its top priority. "The government was committed to ensuring that the benefits of development reach the last person in society," he said.He stated that the state government was fully committed to ensuring that development reaches the most remote and hilly communities."This is a unique initiative to understand the sentiments and problems of people by staying overnight in remote areas. It is the first time that a Chief Minister of the state has gone beyond the confines of government rest houses and stayed overnight in a village home to interact directly with the people", he said.He said that 172 families of Mehla gram panchayat had been identified under the Mukhya Mantri Ka Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojana, which is scheduled to be launched in the state next month. Under the scheme, eligible women aged between 21 and 59 years will receive Rs. 1,500 per month.He clarified that even if a family has three eligible women, all three will be entitled to receive the benefit.The Chief Minister said that a CBSE school would be made functional at Mehla from the next academic session.He said that the government has launched various schemes to enhance farmers’ income. Last year, 107 quintals of naturally grown barley in Pangi valley of Chamba district were purchased at a rate of Rs. 70 per kg, while the purchase rate has been enhanced to Rs. 80 per kg. He added that the procurement price of cow's milk has been increased from Rs. 31 to Rs. 61 per kg and that of buffalo milk from Rs. 46 to Rs. 71 per kg.The state government has also decided to increase the incentive amount for milk producers from Rs. 3 to Rs. 6 per litre to encourage and support milk producers. He said that the state government is also working on a new scheme for the Gaddi community to help them secure better prices for meat.CM Sukhu said that the state government has adopted zero tolerance towards corruption which has helped in generating additional revenue to the state exchequer.The government had to dissolve the Himachal Pradesh Staff Selection Commission (HPSSC) following reports of irregularities and paper leaks, which had deprived meritorious students of a fair opportunity to qualify in competitive examinations. Cases were registered against all the officers and officials involved in the irregularities, who are still behind bars. He said that the recruitment process had now been made completely transparent through computerisation.He added that the state government was filling vacant posts on priority to ensure the smooth functioning of various departments. He said that additional posts in various categories in the health, education and other departments would be filled soon.MLA Neeraj Nayyar, Chairman APMC Chamba Lalit Thakur and senior leaders of the Congress party were also present on the occasion. (ANI)

headline: Earthquake of magnitude 3.2 hits Himachal Pradesh’s Chamba
content: An earthquake of magnitude 3.2 struck Himachal Pradesh’s Chamba district on Friday morning, triggering panic among residents. The tremors were felt at around 6:59 am. According to the available information, the epicentre of the earthquake was located at a depth of approximately 15 kilometres below the Earth's surface. The early morning tremors briefly created panic among people. However, there were no immediate reports of any loss of life or property in the district. Chamba Deputy Commissioner Mukesh Repaswal said that no incident of damage or casualties had been reported due to the earthquake. He added that the administration was closely monitoring the situation. The situation in the district remains normal, and authorities are keeping a close watch on developments.

headline: Technology must be guided by character, commitment and compassion: PGIMER Director
content: Mangaluru: Technology and digital advancements must be guided by character, commitment and compassion to ensure their meaningful use for the welfare of society, said Prof Vivek Lal, Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh.Addressing 16th convocation of Nitte Deemed to be University at Deraakatte, he urged students to draw inspiration from Swami Vivekananda's ideals and uphold the values of character, commitment and compassion, which he described as the three essential pillars for the younger generation."Technology and digital assets have no meaning if there is no island of commitment, compassion and character to harness them," he said, emphasising that India had immense technological capabilities as well as the trust and faith of its patients..Mangaluru woman attacked with iron rod in car; man arrested for attempted murder. Highlighting the importance of patient-centred healthcare, he said the biggest asset of the country was not technology but the faith patients placed in healthcare professionals. He urged medical graduates to remain grateful to patients and dedicate their knowledge and skills to reduce human suffering.Referring to Swami Vivekananda's historic address at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, Prof Lal said the spiritual leader's teachings on character and social responsibility remained relevant even today. He called upon graduates to give back to society in whatever way possible and make service an integral part of their professional lives.He also cautioned students against becoming overconfident about their digital knowledge in the age of artificial intelligence. While acknowledging AI as an extraordinary technological advancement, he stressed the need to ensure that technology was used responsibly and did not become a threat to humanity.Drawing a parallel with the destructive consequences of nuclear technology, he said humanity must ensure that artificial intelligence was not misused. He urged students to follow the ideals of Swami Vivekananda rather than blindly placing their faith in technology.Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, he said the country could achieve the goal even earlier if the younger generation developed an enlightened mindset and worked with a sense of responsibility.Referring to India's rich medical heritage, he recalled the contributions of Sushruta, regarded as the father of surgery, and Charaka, regarded as the father of medicine. He said their prime focus was healing and relieving the suffering of patients.Nitte DU Chancellor N Vishal Hegde presided over the gathering. Degrees were conferred on 1455 graduates.

headline: MY Bharat Chandigarh and Global Youth Federation Organise E-Waste Awareness Campaign Across Three Educational Institutions During BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026
content: MY Bharat Chandigarh, under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, in association with Global Youth Federation, organised a series of awareness programmes on responsible e-waste management across three educational institutions in Chandigarh as part of BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026 (1–7 November 2026). The campaign was organised at Government Senior Secondary School, Sector 15; Government Model High School, Daria; and Post Graduate Government College for Girls, Sector 42, Chandigarh, in collaboration with the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee and Chandigarh Administration, with the support of Karo Sambhav Pvt. Ltd. The initiative aimed to sensitise students and young people about the growing challenge of electronic waste and encourage them to adopt responsible consumption and sustainable lifestyle practices. During the awareness sessions, students were informed about the increasing generation of e-waste from discarded mobile phones, computers, batteries and other electronic equipment. They were also sensitised about the harmful substances present in electronic waste and the adverse effects of improper disposal on human health, soil, water and the environment. Special emphasis was placed on the importance of reducing, repairing and reusing electronic products and ensuring that discarded electronic items are handed over only to authorised recyclers and designated collection channels. Students were also made aware of the environmental risks associated with disposing of e-waste along with regular household garbage or in open spaces and drains. As part of the campaign, students and youth took an environmental pledge to promote responsible e-waste disposal, minimise waste generation, encourage repair and reuse of electronic products, and spread awareness among their families and communities. The campaign also highlighted the message of “Clean, Green and Safer Diwali”, encouraging students and citizens to celebrate the festival in an environmentally responsible manner by adopting eco-friendly practices and reducing unnecessary waste.

headline: India: Why does Delhi fail to tackle its air pollution crisis every year?
content: On a slightly chilly and distinctly smoggy morning in New Delhi, Khushboo Arora was looking for another air purifier for her mother, who has underlying health complications, before the city's air quality deteriorated further. "Already, I am starting to get a recurring headache," she said. "These days when I wake up, I don't feel fresh. As the day progresses, I feel a heaviness in my head, itching in my eye and a constantly parched throat." Not long ago, the unpacking of woolens announced the advent of winter in Delhi. Now, it's the light hum of an air purifier in the corner. Arora said she has already stopped doing yoga in the park and taking her morning walks. She has also filled her house with air-purifying plants and started spraying water mist inside the house to bring down the level of pollution. "My parents look at me like I have gone mad. But I feel people are not realizing the gravity of the situation," she said. Winters in Delhi increasingly follow a familiar pattern: Air quality deteriorates, residents struggle to breathe, emergency restrictions kick in and governments exchange blame. Then the season changes, only for the cycle to repeat the following year.

headline: Massive fire at car showroom in south Delhi; seven injured, 12 rescued
content: New Delhi A massive fire broke out at a Kia car showroom in south Delhi's Saidulajab area on Friday (November 6, 2026), gutting several vehicles and leaving seven people injured, while around 12-15 others were rescued, an official said. The fire has been brought under control and a search operation is under way inside the building to ascertain whether anyone else is trapped or if there are any casualties, Deputy Magistrate Lakshya Singhal said. "Around 3.45 pm, we received information that a Kia showroom opposite the metro station had caught fire. The fire department, police and other agencies were immediately mobilised. The SDM and the SHO also reached the spot," Mr. Singhal said. VIDEO | Delhi: Fire breaks out at a showroom in the Saiyad Ul Ajaib area of Saket. South Delhi DM Lakshya Singhal says, "At around 3:44 pm, we received a call stating that a massive fire had broken out at the Kia showroom in front of Saket Metro Station. As soon as the fire broke out, the Fire Department, Police Department, Traffic Police and CATS Ambulance were all alerted. At the same time, instructions were received from the Chief Minister that a rescue operation must be launched immediately and all possible efforts should be made to save people’s lives. Following the instructions, the rescue operation was conducted effectively. Approximately 12 to 15 people were rescued. Around seven people are injured and are undergoing treatment at Max Hospital and Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital. So far, there are no reports of any casualties or fatalities. The building is being searched again. The Chief Minister is also personally monitoring the entire situation continuously." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)— Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) November 6, 2026 Seven people sustained injuries in the incident, of whom four were admitted to MAX Hospital and three to Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, he said. Around 12-15 people were rescued from the building, with stairs placed against adjoining buildings to evacuate those trapped on the upper floors. Local residents also helped in the rescue operation, Singhal said. "As of now, there have been no casualties. The building is being searched to rule out any casualties," he said, adding that teams from the fire department, police, revenue department, Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), ambulance services and CATS were involved in the operation. The Delhi Fire Services received a call about the blaze at around 3.47 p.m. and initially rushed 10 fire tenders to the spot. Several teams of the Delhi Police and fire department were deployed to contain the flames. Thick plumes of black smoke billowed from the showroom, rising high into the sky and visible from a considerable distance. Several cars parked inside the showroom were engulfed in flames as the fire spread across the premises. The incident also led to a crowd gathering near the showroom, with several passersby stopping to record the blaze on their mobile phones. headline: Delhi: Fire breaks out at car showroom near Saket metro; 16 rescued, two injured
content: New Delhi [India], November 6 (ANI): A fire broke out at a car showroom near Saket Metro in the national capital on Friday afternoon, prompting a swift response from Delhi Police, Fire Brigade and other emergency services.According to Delhi Police, information regarding the fire was received at around 3:45 PM. The showroom falls under the area of PS Mehrauli.With prompt action, approximately 12-15 persons were safely rescued from the top of the building, while four persons were rescued from the backside of the showroom.Two women sustained minor injuries due to smoke inhalation and were immediately shifted to the hospital for medical treatment. Their condition is reported to be stable.Five fire tenders and six ambulances, along with the complete staff of PS Mehrauli, were pressed into service at the spot. The fire has been controlled.No casualties have been reported so far. A total of six vehicles are learnt to have been impacted by the fire, DCP South District said.Another similar incident happened on August 21 when a minor fire broke out at the 'Salman Khan Gym' located on the first floor of M Block Market in Greater Kailash-I, South Delhi, officials said.Delhi Fire Services were alerted around 10:15 PM following reports of smoke and flames originating from the premises. A short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze.Local police personnel arrived at the scene prior to the fire tenders and safely evacuated all occupants inside the establishment, preventing any injuries.Firefighters arrived shortly after and managed to douse the flames, bringing the situation under complete control. (ANI)

headline: 15 rescued as massive fire engulfs Saket car showroom; 7 in hospital
content: New Delhi: A massive fire broke out at a Kia car showroom near Saket metro station Friday afternoon, triggering a multi-agency rescue operation in which around 15 people trapped on the building’s rooftop and shaft area were evacuated by fire personnel.At least seven people experienced breathing difficulties after inhaling smoke and were taken to hospitals, police said, adding that no casualties were reported. Six vehicles were also damaged in the blaze, they said.“The fire broke out around 3.44 pm at the showroom on MB Road, near Saket metro station. Fire officials said a call was received at 3.47 pm and the first fire tender was dispatched within a minute. A total of 13 fire tenders were eventually pressed into service,” DCP (South) Anant Mittal said.As flames engulfed parts of the building, several people moved to the rooftop to escape. Videos circulating on social media showed people attempting to reach an adjoining building through a staircase, while others were seen helping them cross to safety. In one video, a man could be seen carrying a woman on his back across the connecting structure.However, a senior fire official said the main rooftop rescue operation was carried out by firefighters, who used ladders to evacuate those trapped above the staircase shaft.“Those people were above the staircase shaft, and the public had no access there at all. Through a window opening they climbed to the top of the shaft. Our personnel put up a ladder and brought them out,” the official said.He said five to six people were initially found trapped in the shaft area of the building. One man was particularly reluctant to descend using a ladder.“He was terrified and was not ready to come down the ladder. By then, members of the public had placed a ladder from the adjoining building. Two of our personnel were also there, and they brought him across from the other roof,” the official said.South Delhi district magistrate Lakshya Singhal said multiple agencies were mobilised.“As soon as the fire broke out, the fire department, police, traffic police and CATS ambulance services were alerted,” he said.Singhal said around 15 people were rescued and seven injured people are undergoing treatment at Max Hospital and Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital.Police said two women experienced breathing difficulties after inhaling smoke and were taken to a hospital for medical evaluation. Their condition was reported to be stable. The building was searched again to ensure no one remained trapped.The fire was later brought under control, though it caused major traffic disruption on MB Road and adjoining stretches, including Anuvrat Marg and Lala Lajpat Rai Marg.The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained, though officials suspect it may have been triggered by a short circuit.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
